verifications.claim: Peter Alexander is leaving NBC News after 22 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "nearly 22 years" (R2); "A 22-year veteran of NBC News" (R4, R5); "after 22 years" (R6, R7, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state or closely approximate 22 years at NBC News; R1's '20 years' is a minor discrepancy but outweighed by direct matches.

verifications.claim: Peter Alexander will join MS NOW (formerly MSNBC) as an anchor and chief national reporter starting in 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "anchor the 11 a.m. hour at MS NOW as well as hold the title of chief national reporter" (R1); "anchor and chief national reporter for MS NOW" (R3, R4, R5); "formerly MSNBC" (R2, R4); daytime changes "in June" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Role and formerly MSNBC directly supported; starting timeframe implied by March 2026 announcement and June changes but not explicitly '2026'.

verifications.claim: Peter Alexander will anchor the 11 a.m. Eastern hour on MS NOW.

verifications.evidence: "anchor the 11 a.m. hour at MS NOW" (R1); "11 a.m. weekday anchor gig at MS Now" (R2); "anchor the 11 a.m. Eastern hour on MS NOW" (R4, R5); "anchor MS NOW’s 11 a.m. weekday programme" (R6)

verifications.claim: Peter Alexander will serve as a chief national reporter.

verifications.claim: Peter Alexander is leaving his role as NBC News chief White House correspondent.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "chief White House correspondent for NBC News" (R1, R2); "served as chief White House correspondent" (R4, R5); "co-chief White House correspondent" (R7); "signed off from his role as chief White House correspondent" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported; 'co-chief' in one source is consistent with the role.

verifications.claim: Peter Alexander is leaving his role as co-host of Saturday Today.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "co-anchor of the Saturday edition of the Today show" (R1); "co-anchor of “Saturday Today”" (R2, R4, R5); "Saturday Today co-anchor" (R7, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated he is leaving this role across sources.

verifications.claim: Peter Alexander served as NBC's chief White House correspondent.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "chief White House correspondent" (R1, R2, R4, R5); "co-chief White House correspondent" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported in past tense; minor variation with 'co-' is consistent.

verifications.claim: Peter Alexander cited a desire to "challenge himself with something new", as noted by his co-host Laura Jarrett on Today.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: Alexander said: "challenge myself with something new" (R2, R6, R8); Jarrett praised him but did not note this phrase (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Alexander himself cited the phrase on air; no source attributes it as noted by Jarrett.

verifications.claim: Peter Alexander cited a desire to spend more time with his children, as noted by his co-host Laura Jarrett on Today.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: Alexander said: "away from home more than 80 nights... before my daughters lose interest" (R2, R7, R8); Jarrett referenced family time but did not note his citation (R7: "one shot to be Ava and Emma’s dad")
verifications.reasoning: Alexander cited family reasons himself; Jarrett acknowledged it but claim incorrectly attributes the noting to her.
